claim: In the head-to-head comparisons found, choosing cases by learned value beat similarity-based retrieval, with small margins online (Memento parametric vs non-parametric retriever +0.6 to +1.0 F1/accuracy points; CASCADE +2.92 over non-learned retrieval with Qwen3-32B; MemRL +3.6 over MemP); Sarukkai (5 seeds, gpt-4o-mini) finds learned exemplar curation adds about +1 (ALFWorld), +2 (SQL) and +7 to +8 (Wordcraft) over naive accumulation; no paired test with a frozen frontier-class model was found.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B on our agent: similarity top-1 vs similarity plus learned utility top-1, same bank, same number of cases, 5 seeds, report paired difference with CI.
audit_note: Margins quoted as about 0.6 to 3 points omit MemRL +3.6 over MemP (listed in the same evidence) and Sarukkai +8 on Wordcraft; CASCADE uses Qwen3-32B and Sarukkai gpt-4o-mini, so none is a frozen frontier-class test, and "every direct head-to-head" is a claim about the researcher's own search.
claim_before_audit: Choosing a case by learned value beats choosing by similarity alone in every direct head-to-head found, but the margin is small (about 0.6 to 3 points) for frozen frontier-class LLM agents. Gap pass: Sarukkai (5 seeds, gpt-4o-mini) finds learned exemplar value adds +1 (ALFWorld), +2 (SQL), +8 (Wordcraft) over naive accumulation; still no frontier-model paired test.

claim: Most of the gain from case memory comes from having any relevant case at all; the learned-value layer adds a minority. CASCADE: +15.4 of +18.35 over zero-shot is from non-learned case retrieval, +2.92 from the bandit. Memento: the first retrieved case gives +3.7 F1, later ones under 1.
agent_test: Ablate the bank (none / similarity / learned) at fixed tokens and check the ordering of gains.

claim: The exploration bonus is the weakest ingredient of a case bandit. CASCADE with alpha=0 loses only 0.31 average points (66.68 vs 66.37) and beats the full method on 3 of the 9 tasks shown (MIMIC-IV-TLP, SEntFiN, BIRD) in the 32B ablation; no study compares UCB vs Thompson vs greedy Q for case choice. Gap pass: classic simulations (Auer 2002; Kuleshov and Precup 2014) find tuned epsilon-greedy or softmax matches or beats UCB1; Thompson beats LinUCB by under 1 regret point and exploit-only by 1.3 in ads (Chapelle and Li 2011).
agent_test: Run greedy-Q vs UCB vs Thompson on the case bank over a long stream; report regret and final success at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieving more cases does not help: one to four is best. Memento K=1 gives most of the gain and K=4 peaks (64.5 F1); ReasoningBank WebArena-Shopping falls from 49.7 (1 item) to 44.4 (4 items), with 39.0 for none.
agent_test: Sweep K in {0,1,2,4,8} at fixed prompt budget; expect a peak at 1 to 4.

claim: Learned utility needs recurring, similar tasks. MemRL gain over single-task reflection is +9.0 (OS) and +5.1 (ALFWorld) where tasks recur, but a tie on HLE (0.606 vs 0.610, task similarity 0.186). EPR and LLM-R depend on in-domain training data; a learned selection policy transferred to a new task is near the reordering baseline (65.4 vs 63.5). Gap pass: Evo-Memory finds gain correlates with within-dataset task similarity (Pearson 0.717 and 0.563).
agent_test: Test value learning on a recurring-task stream and on a scattered-task stream; expect gain only on the first.
audit_note: MemRL, Active Example Selection (65.4 vs 63.5) and Evo-Memory numbers check out; the EPR and LLM-R in-domain dependence is not supported by any source listed for this claim (it is plausible from those papers), and 65.4 is 1.9 above the reordering baseline.

claim: Blending similarity with learned utility beats either alone: MemRL lambda=0.5 is best (inverted U); pure similarity plateaus and pure Q is volatile. Exact numbers are only in a figure.
agent_test: Sweep the blend weight on our bank; compare with pure similarity and pure utility.

claim: Learned utility correlates with real success on the agent's own stream (MemRL r=0.861, 21.5% to 88.1% across Q bins), but this is in-sample, and about 12% of top-Q memories are failures kept as near-misses.
agent_test: Measure held-out calibration of utility against fresh-task success.

claim: Supervised learned retrieval (label cases by the LM probability of the right answer) beats BM25 and off-the-shelf dense retrieval for in-context examples: EPR dev BREAK 26.0 to 31.9, MTOP 57.0 to 64.2, SMCalFlow 51.4 to 54.3; LLM-R 30-task average 65.7 (1 iteration) vs SBERT 62.1 and random 57.9. Gains stop after about 2 rounds (66.5, then 66.4).
agent_test: Train a small LM-feedback reranker on our task logs; compare with similarity at equal examples.
audit_note: The 57.0 and 51.4 starting points for MTOP and SMCalFlow are the earlier learned retriever CBR (BM25 gets 52.9 and 46.1), so those are gains over the strongest prior retriever, not over BM25.

claim: Learned retrieval has failure cases: LLM-R falls below random on SQuAD (many questions share a passage, so it retrieves near duplicates with low diversity) and its gains on knowledge-intensive tasks (commonsense, reasoning, memorised facts; NQ excepted) are much smaller than the 30-task average; random labels in demonstrations cost only 1.7 points on average for multi-choice and 2.6 for classification (Min et al.), so demonstrations mostly convey format, input distribution and label space. Gap pass: set-level coverage selection (Levy 2023) beats top-k similarity by 2.5 to 6.9 points on GeoQuery with Codex (smallest on the i.i.d. split).
agent_test: Add a diversity term (set-level selection) and test on a task with a duplicate-heavy bank.
audit_note: Wang et al. say the LLM-R gains are substantially smaller on knowledge-intensive tasks (commonsense, reasoning, memorised facts; NQ excepted) and say it helps on Sentiment140; the claim re-labels this as small gains on reading comprehension and sentiment, which the paper does not state (sentiment is +41 over random in its table). SQuAD below random, Min et al. 1.7/2.6, and Levy 2.5 to 6.9 check out.
claim_before_audit: Learned retrieval has failure cases: LLM-R falls below random on SQuAD (near duplicates, low diversity) and gains are small on reading comprehension and sentiment; random labels in demonstrations cost only 1.7 to 2.6 points on average, so demonstrations mostly teach format. Gap pass: set-level coverage selection (Levy 2023) beats top-k similarity by 2.5 to 6.9 points on GeoQuery with Codex, less on i.i.d.

claim: Set-level selection (modelling interactions and diversity among chosen cases) beats scoring cases one by one: CEIL gains about 2 to 5 points over EPR on GeoQuery; efficiency table average 64.86 (EPR) vs 68.86 (CEIL n=100). Levy 2023 independently supports set-level coverage (Cover-LS vs Top-K 91.4 vs 88.9 i.i.d., 81.6 vs 74.7 template split).
agent_test: Compare top-K by score with a diversity-aware set picker at the same K.

claim: Which examples go in the prompt changes accuracy a lot on small old models (over 30 points spread on GPT-2), and a learned selection policy helps small models but the benefit shrinks with larger ones. The learned policy (71.4 same task) roughly equals best-of-10 random draws (72.5).
agent_test: Measure the spread of random case sets on our model; if spread is small, a value learner has little to win.

claim: Case-value learning needs nonzero base competence; when zero-shot success is near zero all methods fail (Qwen3-4B on MIMIC-IV-MR), and CASCADE keeps only successful cases.
agent_test: Find the minimum base success rate at which our case bank pays; do not bank from tasks the model never solves.

claim: Value-tagged case memory beat similarity-only memory for a frozen LLM agent in early REMEMBERER work, but by small margins (WebShop success 0.39 vs ReAct 0.36; WikiHow reward 2.63 vs 2.50), with no significance test.
agent_test: Replicate with a modern model; expect a smaller gain.

claim: Naive verbatim retrieval can hurt: Dynamic Cheatsheet retrieval-only (DR) dropped GPT-4o on Game of 24 (10 to 6) and MMLU-Pro Eng (53.2 to 48.8); curated memory gained on Game of 24 (93 to 99) but not on MMLU-Pro Eng, where GPT-4o fell under every variant. Memp: random sampling beat query-keyed retrieval for GPT-4o on TravelPlanner (74.59 vs 73.38).
agent_test: Compare raw-case retrieval against curated or distilled strategies on our agent.
audit_note: Numbers are right (Game of 24 10 to 6, MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 to 48.8 under DR; Memp 74.59 vs 73.38), but curated memory did not gain on MMLU-Pro Eng for GPT-4o (DC-Cu 44.0, DC-RS 51.2, both below baseline 53.2); it gained only on Game of 24 (93 and 99).
claim_before_audit: Naive verbatim retrieval can hurt: Dynamic Cheatsheet retrieval-only dropped GPT-4o on Game of 24 (10 to 6) and MMLU-Pro Eng (53.2 to 48.8) while curated memory gained. Memp: random sampling beat query-keyed retrieval for GPT-4o on TravelPlanner (74.59 vs 73.38).

claim: Reward design matters when learning from outcomes: a judge-based reward raised judge score but lowered F1 (33.69 vs 41.05) in Memory-R1; ReasoningBank success labels come from an LLM judge of about 72.7% accuracy. Gap pass: Xiong 2025 shows an untuned LLM success judge can leave a raw-record bank below the fixed bank (C1 36.92 vs 40.11 on AgentDriver), while a judge tuned on 300 runs recovers (47.37); ReasoningBank memory degrades only from about 52 to 47.6 even at random labels.
agent_test: Use verifiable outcome signals for case value where possible; audit label noise.
audit_note: Fig 8 values are read from a plot (about 52 to 47.6); cross-benchmark comparison is loose but hedged.

claim: Bandit-style budgeted evaluation beats uniform for choosing prompts from a pool (TRIPLE +9.7 to +17.4% at 10 evals per prompt; INSTINCT best on 11 of 20 tasks), but these test prompts, not cases, and gains fade with budget.
agent_test: Use successive halving to evaluate a small set of candidate cases per query type.

claim: Apart from CASCADE, no study found applies UCB or Thompson sampling with regret reporting to case choice for a frozen frontier LLM. CASCADE is a preprint, unreplicated, with self-reported 5-seed results. Gap pass confirms: still none found.
agent_test: Independent replication of CASCADE on one of its public tasks.

claim: Theory: CASCADE regret splits into coverage gap and retrieval regret with sublinear total, but needs i.i.d. queries, Lipschitz case value and a fixed LLM success chance; real agent streams violate i.i.d.
agent_test: Test drift: shuffled vs ordered task stream and measure retrieval regret.

claim: Learned-retrieval layers saturate: Memento bank saturates at about 3k items; LLM-R stops after 2 iterations; the CASCADE gain over NP-CBR shrinks under ReAct (+0.98 ALFWorld, +3.15 ScienceWorld).
agent_test: Track marginal gain of each added learned layer; stop adding when under 1 point.
audit_note: Memento says the case bank saturates with about 3k training data (not 3k items strictly); minor.

claim: About two thirds of MemRL's runtime advantage over plain RAG is not present on held-out tasks with a frozen bank: 8.15 points runtime vs 2.8 points transfer on four shared benchmarks (my recomputation, different splits, no seeds).
agent_test: Hold out a stream with no repeated items and freeze the bank; report gain vs similarity-only on the same backbone.

claim: Learned per-case value as a greedy empirical success rate (min 3 retrievals) is enough to beat naive accumulation on fresh test tasks in a 5-seed study: +1 to +8 points over similarity-retrieved accumulated trajectories with gpt-4o-mini; curated bank equals pass@2 to pass@5 of the fixed bank at test cost.
agent_test: Replicate with a frontier backbone and paired seeds; give uncurated and curated banks equal total tokens.

claim: Success-label quality decides whether outcome-based bank growth helps: with raw records an untuned LLM judge leaves the bank below a small fixed bank (AgentDriver 36.92 vs 40.11), a judge fine-tuned on 300 runs reaches 47.37 and a strict evaluator 51.00. For distilled lessons the cost of label noise is smaller (about 52 to 47.6 at random labels).
agent_test: Measure the judge's accuracy on a sample of own runs before using it as a value label; prefer verifiable outcomes.
audit_note: Cross-benchmark comparison (AgentDriver vs WebArena) is loose; numbers match.

claim: Utility-based deletion (drop records with low average downstream success, at least n retrievals) helps with a strict evaluator (CIC-IoT 89.60 vs 85.40; EHRAgent 42.06 vs 38.67) but is unstable with a coarse one (AgentDriver 34.00 vs 36.92); periodic pruning cuts memory to a quarter to a third with small loss.
agent_test: Use periodic pruning by retrieval count always; add utility-based eviction only when labels are checked.

claim: Classic bandit sources do not support a UCB bonus as the default: tuned epsilon-greedy almost always did best in Auer 2002; softmax and epsilon-greedy beat UCB1 in most of 12 instances in Kuleshov and Precup 2014 (softmax beat its closest competitor by 10% to 100% in regret); Chapelle and Li 2011 found Thompson sampling beat UCB and epsilon-greedy in simulation and in contextual ad and news experiments. Auer 2002 and Kuleshov and Precup use stationary context-free bandits.
agent_test: If an exploration rule is wanted, use Thompson on per-case Beta posteriors; compare against plain greedy with small epsilon.
audit_note: Chapelle and Li is not context-free: it includes contextual bandit experiments (display-ad CTR with features, LinUCB, news recommendation), so "All are stationary and context-free" is wrong; also the 10% to 100% figure is Boltzmann versus its closest competitor, not versus UCB1, and Chapelle and Li call Thompson sampling highly competitive rather than strongest.
claim_before_audit: Classic bandit sources do not support a UCB bonus as the default: tuned epsilon-greedy almost always best in Auer 2002; epsilon-greedy and softmax beat UCB1 in most of 12 instances in Kuleshov and Precup 2014 (10% to 100% lower regret); Thompson sampling is the strongest simple stochastic rule in Chapelle and Li 2011. All are stationary and context-free.

claim: Under drifting case value, plain running means lag. Theory: no policy beats about sqrt(T) regret under abrupt changes; discounted or sliding-window UCB reach it within a log factor. Practical result: addition plus utility deletion kept performance close to the no-shift run after a stream shift in two agents, with no tests of how far tasks drift.
agent_test: Use a window or discount on case value estimates and test one deliberate task-family switch.
audit_note: The no-tests-of-drift-extent part is an absence claim not checkable from the sources; Evo-Memory not needed for the wording.

claim: Storing failures raw is risky, storing them as lessons is not: Evo-Memory baselines degrade when failed trajectories are stored unfiltered; ReasoningBank gains 46.5 to 49.7 with failures while AWM falls 44.4 to 42.2. Aamodt and Plaza (1994) already proposed failure cases as reminders. No study ablates failures under a learned selector.
agent_test: Store failures as short avoid-lessons attached to a class, not as retrievable examples.
audit_note: Last sentence (no study ablates failures under a learned selector) is an absence claim, not checkable.

claim: Best-of-N repeated sampling and case-value learning compete for the same tokens, and the winner depends on having a verifier: with one, coverage rose 15.9% to 56% (SWE-bench Lite, 250 samples); without one, majority vote moved 40.50% to 41.41% over 100 to 10,000 samples. No equal-token comparison against learned case value exists.
agent_test: Equal-token test: N samples with a verifier vs one sample with a learned-value case; same tasks.
audit_note: The two Brown et al. figures come from different tasks (SWE-bench Lite vs MATH with Llama-3-8B); wording does not say so but numbers are right.
